entities.summary: The port of Antwerp is the port of the city of Antwerp, Belgium. It is located in Flanders, mainly in the province of Antwerp, but also partially in East Flanders. It is a seaport in the heart of Europe accessible to capesize ships. It is Europe's second-largest seaport, after that of Rotterdam. Antwerp stands at the upper end of the tidal estuary of the Scheldt. The estuary is navigable by ships of more than 100,000 Gross Tons as far as 80 km inland. Like the Port of Hamburg, the Port of Antwerp's inland location provides a more central location in Europe than the majority of North Sea ports.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a major seaport in Western Europe, the Port of Antwerp played a crucial role in trade and commerce during the Middle Ages, facilitating the exchange of goods between the Hanseatic League and other European powers. Its strategic location allowed it to become one of the busiest ports in Europe by the 14th century.
